root_cause: At 10:04 I taught the monitor to probe the DAY'S HIGH/LOW for trigger arms, so a spike that pierced a breakout level and retraced inside one 60s poll would still register. WRONG for a STOP on a position opened midday: BANKNIFTY's day high 57,964 was set ~09:30, nearly 3 hours BEFORE the 12:14 entry, so any ABOVE stop below that level fires instantly and permanently.
why_it_did_not_cost_anything: I verify price before acting on a signal rather than trading the alert. LTP was 57,770.35 vs stop 57,820 -> not hit -> position held.
fix: Trigger arms now carry an explicit probe mode. probe=BREAKOUT uses the day extreme; probe=LTP (the DEFAULT, i.e. the safe choice) uses last price only. All 7 live management arms reset to probe=LTP and the false fire cleared. Monitor restarted (old task stopped first to avoid duplicate writers).
generalisation: An extreme-based probe is only valid for a level that was armed BEFORE the extreme was set. Any level armed mid-session must be evaluated on LTP, or on an extreme measured since arming — never on the session extreme.
note: The book-level stop check (live_book stop_level) was always LTP-based and correct; the buggy path was the duplicate trigger arm.

topic: ENGINEERED CAS — built the closing-auction signal instead of waiting for NSE to publish one
premise: A closing auction is order-flow IMBALANCE driving the closing print. NSE publishes no usable feed (key=CAS = 200/zero rows, two days). But the OPTION BOOK shows that imbalance directly, and platform_core/data/live/option_flow_shadow.py has been logging it every minute since 07-28.
formula: book_imb(side) = (SUM bid_qty - SUM ask_qty)/(SUM bid_qty + SUM ask_qty) over ATM+/-2 strikes; net_book_imb = call_imb - put_imb, range [-2,+2].

all_day.verdict: NOTHING — and this null is what proves the test is not rigged

last_hour.verdict: CONTRARIAN and consistent across all three indices independently

mechanism: Displayed resting depth is liquidity PROVISION, not aggression. Heavy resting bids get filled INTO selling, so price trades through the heavy side. Hence FADE the book. The effect being ABSENT all day and present only near the close is exactly the closing-flow structure, not a blanket anomaly.
HONEST_CAVEATS: Entry time is UNSTABLE: 14:15 gives -18,768 while 14:30 gives +12,116. A 15-min shift flipping the sign is overfit-shaped.
I scanned 16 parameter combinations and am quoting the best — multiple-comparisons bias.
3 correlated symbols x 8 days means EFFECTIVE n is ~8, not 20.
BUT: the control refutes the obvious alternative — baselines LOSE (always-PE -5,508) and the mean index move was +2.3bps (slightly UP), so this is not closing drift.
decision: Take a SMALL live test at the 14:30 window. Size = 1 lot. This is a measurement, not a bet — the instability above forbids sizing.
execution_design: scripts/claude_cas_read.py reads the VM logger's OWN series rather than recomputing locally. My local re-implementation (claude_cas_signal.py) reproduces the SIGN but not the magnitude (different bid/ask-quantity source), and the validation was done on the logger's series — so read that one and replication error goes to zero.

specific_lesson: BREADTH CONFIRMS A BREAK ONLY IF THE DAY IS NOT ALREADY ESTABLISHED AS RANGE-BOUND. On a range day, synchronized dips across indices are what a range TEST looks like — breadth is exactly what you see at the bottom of a range, so it cannot distinguish a break from a test. The discriminator I needed was RANGE EXPANSION (a widening true range / vol expansion), which never happened: SENSEX range sat at 0.39-0.42% all session.
counterfactual: Requiring range expansion (e.g. session range > 0.55% or a VIX uptick) as a second condition would have vetoed this entry. That is the filter to test, NOT a lower conviction threshold.
